hints.S58_A1: The dash explains it: STILL COOL AND DEWY from the EARLY DELIVERY, and they are compared to A MORNING BREEZE. Ask: which word describes vegetables just brought in, not yet limp? Price, noise and weight are not the point.
hints.S58_A2: After the FOOD BLOGGER visited, PEOPLE QUEUED FOR OVER AN HOUR. Ask: which idiom means everybody is discussing it? 'A piece of cake' means easy, 'out of the blue' means sudden, and 'under the weather' means unwell.
hints.S58_A3: The fishmonger is GENEROUS: the EXTRA PRAWNS come with every purchase and nobody pays a cent for them. Ask: which phrasal verb means to hand something over for free? 'Sell' asks for money; 'keep' and 'hide' hold on to it.
hints.S58_A4: STALLS STRETCHED FROM ONE END OF THE HALL TO THE OTHER, selling SPICES, FRUIT AND CLOTH. Ask: which word names a busy market hall? A library holds books, a clinic treats the sick, and a playground is for games.
hints.S58_A5: She meets her REGULARS WITH A WARM SMILE and remembers each person's USUAL ORDER. Ask: which verb keeps that friendly direction? 'Ignored', 'avoided' and 'confused' would all push a customer away.
hints.S58_B1: The subject is SOMEBODY, not the stall behind it. Words like somebody and nobody count as one person, even in a crowded market. Ask: in the present tense, does a singular subject take the plain verb, or the verb wearing -s?
hints.S58_B2: 'HAS' is already printed, and the selling has lasted FOR OVER TWENTY YEARS. Ask: which form follows 'has' to build a present perfect - the plain verb, the -s form, the -ing form, or the past participle? This verb is irregular.
hints.S58_B3: THAN weighs one fish stall against one other - just two of them - and the adjective has three syllables. Ask: can a long adjective take -er? 'Most' is for a whole group, and 'very' compares nothing at all.
hints.S58_B4: ANOTHER REGULAR ARRIVED suddenly, cutting across a job that was already half done. Ask: which choice shows an action still in progress in the PAST? The vendor had not finished when the interruption came.
hints.S58_B5: THE MORNING CROWD HAD BOUGHT THEM ALL, so hardly any are left - and mangoes can be counted one by one. Ask: which choice means 'not many' and belongs with countable plural nouns? 'Little' and 'much' need uncountable things.
hints.S58_B6: The statement is positive, and its verb is a present perfect stretching OVER FORTY YEARS. Ask: does a tag echo the helping verb already in the sentence, or borrow 'did'? And after a positive statement, which way does the tag flip?
hints.S58_B7: The PORK RIBS could not marinate themselves - someone laid them in the SPECIAL MARINADE for three hours. Ask: which choice is passive (the subject receives the action) and set in the past? 'Ribs' is plural, so choose the plural helper.
hints.S58_B8: ASKED THE CUSTOMER = a reported request, and it is about THE NEXT MORNING. Ask: after 'asked + person', which form follows - the plain verb, the -ing form, or 'to' + verb? Only one choice is a full infinitive.
hints.S58_C1: FIVE O'CLOCK is an exact point on the clock face. Ask: which box preposition goes with exact clock times? 'In' belongs with months and 'on' with days - neither can pin down a single minute.
hints.S58_C2: SUNDAY is a day of the week, and the blank sits right in front of it. Ask: which box preposition partners days and dates? The word for exact clock times and the word for months are both needed elsewhere.
hints.S58_C3: DURIAN SEASON arrives with a whole month: JUNE. Ask: which box preposition goes with months, years and seasons? The word for days of the week and the word for exact clock times will not do here.
hints.S58_C4: THIRTY YEARS measures a length of time, not a starting point. Ask: which box preposition answers the question 'how long?' A word that counts backwards from today would need the buying to be over and done with.
hints.S58_C5: OVER FIFTY YEARS counts backwards from today, right up to the moment you are reading. Ask: which box word sits AFTER the length of time rather than in front of it? Look carefully at where the blank has been placed.
hints.S58_C6: The produce must reach the stall before TWELVE HOURS have passed - the sentence adds OF HARVESTING. Ask: which box preposition means 'inside that time limit, not after it'? A plain month-word would flip the meaning to 'after'.
hints.S58_C7: The smell lasts FROM DAWN UNTIL CLOSING - every hour of the day, with no gaps at all. Ask: which box word means 'all the way through, from beginning to end'? A short word for months could never stretch that far.
hints.S58_C8: The promise sets a deadline: NEVER LATER THAN THAT. Ask: which box preposition means 'at that time or sooner'? The word for an exact clock time would fix the orders to one single minute and no earlier.
hints.S58_D1: EACH one is RUN BY A FAMILY who sell just one type of food. Ask: which box word names a single small shop inside a market hall? The person who runs it and the goods laid out on it are different things.
hints.S58_D2: The blank ARRANGES the produce, so it must be a person, not a place or a thing. Ask: which box word names the seller who runs a stall? Match the word to what the sentence says it DOES.
hints.S58_D3: The produce is set out in an ATTRACTIVE arrangement SO CUSTOMERS CAN SEE EVERYTHING CLEARLY. The blank follows 'an attractive', so it must be a noun. Ask: which box word names goods laid out to be looked at?
hints.S58_D4: Shoppers COMPARE PRICES and ASK FOR A DISCOUNT when they buy a lot. The blank follows 'know how to', so it must be a verb. Ask: which box word means to argue politely for a lower price?
hints.S58_D5: The clue follows the comma: ONLY AVAILABLE AT CERTAIN TIMES OF THE YEAR. The blank comes after 'are', so it must describe the items. Ask: which box word means 'sold only at one time of the year'?
hints.S58_E1: The underlined verb belongs to THE VEGETABLES, laid out on WIDE BAMBOO TRAYS - many of them, not one. Ask: which past form goes with a plural subject? Singular and plural verbs can never be swapped.
hints.S58_E2: 'HEAR' is what you do with your EARS, but Grandma is pointing at a spot - this stall, NOT AT THE SUPERMARKET. Ask: which spelling means 'at this place'? Choose by meaning, never by sound.
hints.S58_E3: 'PEIR' has its two vowels the wrong way round. Ask: which letter comes first in this word, the I or the E? The rule is I before E, except after C - the same order as in belief, niece and thief.
hints.S58_E4: The underlined word tells us HOW the uncle CALLED to passing customers. Ask: after an action verb, do we use an adjective or an adverb? Adjectives describe nouns; adverbs of manner take an -ly tail.
hints.S58_E5: The TRAYS belong to the VENDORS - many sellers, many trays. Ask: does a bare -s by itself ever mean 'belonging to'? When the owners are plural and already end in -s, only a mark of punctuation is missing.
hints.S58_F1: 'AS SOON AS' means 'the very moment that', so one event triggers the other. Ask: which sentence is the trigger and which is the response? And may a future 'will' ever appear inside the 'as soon as' half?
hints.S58_F2: Sentence B is still a question: 'HOW MUCH DO THE VEGETABLES COST?' Ask: when it is reported, does the helper 'do' stay, and does the subject come before the verb or after it? Reported speech uses statement order.
